title: Execution-Signature Recycling: Deduplicating Unit-Test Failure Feedback for Test-Time Code Scaling

contributions.purpose: Reduce redundant execution feedback across candidates in best-of-N code generation.
contributions.mechanism: Execution-Signature Recycling (ESR) clusters candidate programs by their execution signature (set of failing tests and error types) and conditions subsequent generations on a compact, deduplicated failure bank in a two-round exploration/exploitation procedure.
contributions.evaluation: On HumanEval+ with Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct under a 16-generation budget, ESR achieves the highest mean Pass@1 (87.60%).
contributions.domain: Test-time scaling / inference-time compute for code generation.
contributions.source_quote: We propose ESR, a method that aggregates execution feedback across candidates using signature-based clustering and provides deduplicated failure information to guide subsequent generations.

contributions.purpose: Provide a statistically rigorous evaluation of the method.
contributions.mechanism: Uses pre-registered decision rules and paired bootstrap confidence intervals across multiple random seeds.
contributions.evaluation: 95% confidence interval on the ESR vs Self-Debug difference is [-0.81, 2.24], which includes zero.
contributions.domain: Test-time scaling / inference-time compute for code generation.
contributions.source_quote: We conduct a rigorous evaluation with pre-registered decision rules and paired bootstrap confidence intervals across multiple random seeds.

contributions.purpose: Report a negative result about cross-sample feedback aggregation.
contributions.mechanism: Compares ESR against a per-sample Self-Debug baseline under identical generation budget.
contributions.evaluation: ESR (87.60%) does not significantly outperform Self-Debug (86.99%); difference CI includes zero, evidence that simpler feedback suffices for strong models.
contributions.domain: Test-time scaling / inference-time compute for code generation.
contributions.source_quote: We report a negative result: ESR does not significantly outperform per-sample self-debugging on HumanEval+, providing evidence that simpler feedback approaches may be sufficient for strong models.

self_declared_provenance.quote: Self-debugging methods (Chen et al., 2023) use error messages and tracebacks to iteratively refine failing candidates, while approaches like Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023) and Self-Refine (Madaan et al., 2023) maintain memory of past failures to guide future attempts. However, these methods typically operate on individual candidates, refining each based on its own execution feedback without sharing information across candidates.

notes: Explicit negative result: ESR does not significantly outperform Self-Debug baseline (87.60% vs 86.99%, 95% CI [-0.81, 2.24] includes zero). Authors frame the negative result as a contribution.
